findings.title: Browser API key is persisted in localStorage
findings.what: The accepted BYO design stores the user's Anthropic API key in localStorage. Any successful same-origin XSS or compromised same-origin script can read and exfiltrate this long-lived credential; exempting the path from the server chokepoint does not mitigate client-side credential theft.
findings.fix: Revise the BYO contract to keep the key in memory for the active operation or session only, require explicit re-entry after reload, and require a restrictive CSP with no untrusted script execution. Do not persist the raw key in localStorage or another script-readable durable store.
findings.acceptance: The ADR no longer permits raw API-key persistence in localStorage; it specifies memory-only/session-bounded handling and CSP requirements, and an automated browser check proves reload clears the credential and no durable web-storage entry contains it.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the accepted Decision at lines 30-44 and the security consequences/rejected alternatives at lines 135-173 in immutable baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The server chokepoint and OAuth invariant protect server egress but do not protect a script-readable browser credential; no mitigation for localStorage theft is stated.
